story_locks.cover_story_branch_A: Never planned on screen: the planning beat (s1a01 b4) was cut for length, and one line in s1a01 b3 sets it. It is played instead. Aditya was running his own con on the bride's side, brass for gold and a house rented for a month, so two thieves married each other; he woke because a pharmacist knows the taste; now he wants a cut and can give the bureau what it lacks, powder that works. Carried by s1a01 b6 (the brass shown to Billu), b7 (the pharmacist's offer, and Kiran's reason to Mausi for the all-clear) and b10 (Mausi laughs at the brass).

code.prompt: Mausi asks whether the son-in-law has drunk his milk.
code.all_clear: 'पी लिया': Billu brings the car to the door at 3 am.
code.alarm: 'दूध फट गया': Billu takes the boys up.
code.anything_else: Any other answer, or no answer, also sends them up.
code.heard_by_viewer: s1e02 b9, in Mausi's own voice to Billu in the lane, before the 2 am call and out of Aditya's hearing. The clock is set up in s1e01 b5.
code.who_knows: Kiran, Mausi and Billu know both phrases. Aditya knows the 2 am call, and so the milk question, is the gang's check on the groom, and he expects the yes (s1e02 b4). He does not know that an alarm phrase exists, or that any other answer or silence counts as one, until Kiran tells him in s1a01 b3 or until he hears it said in s1b01 b1. In branch A Kiran tells Mausi why she gave the all-clear with the groom awake (s1a01 b7).
code.pinned_message: Not used. The pitch's pinned message is dropped: the code is carried in audio and on the ballot.

story_locks.sedative: Never named, never quantified, never shown being prepared beyond a paper fold tapped over a glass. Aditya talks about dose as a pharmacist would, with no numbers. The con is drama, not a method.
story_locks.phones: Kiran's SIM is out from before s1e01 b4 until Aditya puts it back in s1e02 b4, so the only call she takes on screen is Mausi's at 2 am. Mausi is a voice on a phone, fully voiced, in every shared-episode appearance.
story_locks.rekha: Invented by Kiran in s1e02 b4. No such person exists. In branch A the lie frays (s1a01 b10, s1a02 b3); in s1a03 b2 Mausi, who has never heard the name, backs it to cover for Kiran ('रेखा? वो तो दो साल पहले भाग गई, दामाद जी।'); and Kiran ends it herself (s1a03 b3). In branch B it is never repeated; Mausi's fate in s1b03 b6 echoes it.
story_locks.names: Aditya calls her 'Sneha' through both shared episodes, and says the name at least once in s1e01 before b5. The viewer first hears 'किरण' from Mausi, on Billu's phone in the lane (s1e01 b5), out of Aditya's hearing, so the viewer knows 'Sneha' is false before Aditya promises 'Sneha' she can walk (s1e02 b7). On the 2 am speaker call Mausi says only बेटा, never the name. Aditya first hears 'Kiran' from Billu: s1a01 b6 or s1b01 b4. In s1a02 b5 Mausi says she gave her that name ('किरण नाम मैंने रखा था तेरा। याद है?'), and 'Tulsi' pays it off: spoken once, by her, in s1a03 b10, and never in branch B. 'Pooja' may be spoken once, in s1a03 b3.
story_locks.money: ₹18 lakh, held by Mausi, promised with the last wedding. First said in s1e01 b6. In branch A Mausi still promises it (s1a02 b5) and the truth is never confirmed. In branch B it was never going to be paid (s1b02 b7).
story_locks.mohit: His death is spoken once as fact (s1e01 b10) and referred to afterwards. It is never pictured, re-enacted or described further.

s1e01 b10 and b11, Aditya: 'मोहित ग्यारह दिन बाद पंखे से लटका मिला।' and 'मुझे ये हाथ चाहिए।'
s1e02 b10, Mausi: 'दामाद जी ने दूध पी लिया, बेटा?'

s1b01 b8, Mausi: 'दरवाज़ा खोलिए, दामाद जी।'
kept_apart_in_the_two_finales: 'आपने ही सिखाया है' is said in s1a03 b5 only. s1b03 b6 has its own line: 'हिसाब अब मैं रखूँगी, मौसी।'

'The boy turned out weak' is said in s1b01 b10 only. In s1a03 b1 the fact that Mausi knew comes out through Kiran's question and Mausi's silence. The fact itself is fixed before the choice and surfaces in both branches.

Of the two finales, only branch B's has Mausi reach for Kiran's wrist (s1b03 b4), to turn Aditya on her. In s1a03 she covers for Kiran, never reaches for the wrist and never offers the hand; Kiran refuses the cover, so the confession is her own choice.

end_of_s1e01.viewer: Everything Aditya has said, and that the scarred hand is Kiran's. That the gang calls her Kiran, so 'Sneha' is a false name. The gang's clock: a call at two, a car at three.
end_of_s1e01.kiran: Who Aditya is, why he is here, that Mohit is dead, and that he is hunting her own wrist.
end_of_s1e01.aditya: The gang's method; that 'Sneha' is one of its brides; that a 'brother' waits outside. Not her real name, not that she was Mohit's bride.

end_of_s1e02.viewer: The code and what each phrase does; that there is no third answer; what Aditya will do to the owner of the hand; that 'Rekha' is a lie; that Mausi packed the mathri.
end_of_s1e02.kiran: All of the above except Mausi's exact words to Billu, which she has no need to hear: it is her own code.
end_of_s1e02.aditya: That a girl called Rekha with a burnt wrist sits with Mausi (false). That a 2 am call must be answered, and that the call and its milk question are the gang's check on the groom, to which he expects a yes. He does not know that an alarm phrase exists, or that any other answer or silence counts as one. He has not seen the skin under her cuff, and he still calls her Sneha.
end_of_s1e02.mausi_and_billu: Nothing is wrong yet. They do not know the groom is awake, who he is, or that the door is padlocked.

knowledge.branch_A_only: Aditya learns of the alarm phrase (s1a01 b3). Mausi learns the groom was awake and why Kiran still gave the all-clear (s1a01 b7). Mausi learns who he is and whose hand he is hunting from the photograph (s1a02 b8), threatens to say it (s1a02 b9), then chooses to cover for Kiran and backs the 'Rekha' lie (s1a03 b1, b2). Kiran learns from Mausi's silence that she knew about Mohit (s1a03 b1). Aditya learns the truth about the hand from Kiran, who refuses the cover (s1a03 b3). Whether the ₹18 lakh was real is never settled.
knowledge.branch_B_only: Aditya learns there was an alarm phrase when he hears it said (s1b01 b1). Mausi learns who he is from the notebook and photograph (s1b01 b10). Kiran learns Mausi knew about Mohit (s1b01 b10), what 'handling him' means (s1b01 b11), and that the money and the last wedding were lies (s1b02 b7). Aditya learns the truth about the hand from Mausi (s1b03 b4). 'Rekha' and 'Tulsi' are never spoken.

register.convention: Hindi in Devanagari and English words in Latin script in the same line; spoken forms (ये, वो), never यह or वह. Names in Devanagari in the Hindi script.
register.aditya: Educated small-city pharmacist. English nouns that are natural to him: dose, sedative, SIM, speaker, photo, bureau, police, licence, reception.
register.kiran: Small-city Hinglish: phone, party, plan, police, time, tension. As 'Sneha', fewer English words and more आप.
register.mausi_and_billu: Hindi-heavy, with the trade's English only: party, booking, advance, biodata, photo, parlour, bureau.
register.chhoti: Phone English: selfie, reel, status, okay, bye.
register.one_word_per_object: पुड़िया for the paper fold (sachet in English). चूड़ा for the chooda. ताला for the padlock and चाबी for the key. दूध for the milk. हिसाब for the accounts, and ledger only in Aditya's mouth. गाड़ी for the car.
register.english_version: A full adaptation by the same cast in Indian English. The code must still sound like a mother's check-in: 'Did Damaad ji drink his milk, beta?', 'Yes, Mausi. He drank it.', 'Mausi... the milk has split.' Keep Mausi, beta, Damaad ji, Jijaji, Didi, chooda, mathri, lakh.
register.performance_flags: Mausi's phone and through-the-door lines are warm and fully voiced, never whispered, and the bed ducks under 'दामाद जी ने दूध पी लिया, बेटा?'. s1e02 ends on Mausi's repeated question, 'हाँ बेटा? पी लिया?', and Kiran's in-breath: a breath with no word in it, recorded as a breath and not as a cut-off 'मौसी'. Each branch opener carries her whole locked line in one take.

production_locks: Stills with camera moves only. Action is single strong images: hands, faces, objects. Nothing depends on continuous movement.
Kiran: plain red saree, no heavy jewellery, block henna, chooda on both forearms; then the same chooda, henna and hair with the grey salwar-kurta. Bare forearm only in the two endings.

s1e01 b1 to b10: the left forearm is never in frame uncovered. It is under the fall of the pallu or against her body, and she uses only her right hand at the tray, the door and the phone. Its stack stays pushed up, out of sight, until b11 shows the scar and slides the stack down over it.
Aditya: glasses and the brass key on its red thread in every shot, including lying with his eyes shut.
The two leads are clothed and apart in the bedroom. The only touch is hand on wrist. She changes clothes off screen behind the almirah door. No intimacy staging.
Mohit's death is never pictured. Mohit is only a hand in a photograph.

'The boys' are never faces (D-005 change 17: locked to hands, backs and silhouettes, not given a reference sheet). In all 11 of their beats they are backs, hands, boots and backlit shapes, with any head cropped, turned away or in full shadow. Two fixed shapes so the silhouettes repeat: heavy-set, shaved head, maroon track jacket; thin, checked shirt, cloth cap. Billu is the only face among the three. They never speak.
The police are an engine, light through shutter slats, a khaki sleeve and a pen. Invented force, no crest, no flag, no readable board.
All readable text is an overlay: phone screens, the time, the shop name, ledger rows.

The bedroom is broken up with inserts (glass, paper fold, padlock, key, photograph, phone, SIM, brass set, bag pocket, window) and at least one cut to Billu in the lane in each shared episode (s1e01 b5; s1e02 b9 and b12).
No set-up is held past 8 seconds. Beats that run longer name more than one set-up.
No crowd anywhere: the wedding is over before the story starts, the lane is empty, the bureau is shut to customers.
No weapon is shown on anyone in any episode.
Mausi is not seen in s1e01 or s1e02; her first image is s1a01 b9 or s1b01 b9. Her reference sheet is still needed before scripts.

English verbs belong in the Hindi lines where a speaker would use them, not only English nouns (plan section 3): lock करना, call करना, check करना, book करना and the like. The anchor lines quoted in this bible are light on them; writers may add them anywhere except inside story_locks.locked_lines.
content_notes: Every character is an adult. Kiran being taken from her uncle's house at fourteen is backstory in a line or two, never shown.
One suicide, in the past: stated once as fact and never pictured or described further.
A plan to kill a man and pass it off as his own act is spoken as intent in branch B. No method, substance or quantity is given, and it does not happen.
The sedative is never named or measured.
The police force, its uniform details and the chowki are invented; no crest, no national flag, no real people, no real bureau.
A temple wedding is mentioned and a temple step appears in one photograph; no deity, ritual or community is shown or named.
No intimacy staging, no nudity, no gore, no weapon.
